Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH"
Document: "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH"

These are genuinely different company names. Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik (HBM) is a company that rebranded/merged — actually, HBM became "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" after the merger of HBM with Brüel & Kjær under Spectris. So historically, HBM was renamed to Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH around 2019-2021. The certificate issued in 2021 by PTB would list the current legal name "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" while the register (OIML-CS database) may have the older name "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH".

Per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

The names are genuinely different strings — not spelling drift or suffix drift. Even though they refer to the same corporate entity historically (a rename), the rule says genuinely different company names = different-entity, best_value = document's. Hmm, but "same-entity" verdict would apply for spelling drift etc. The rename means the legal entity changed its name; the certificate as legal instrument carries the name at time of issue. The rule's decision procedure: spelling drift, suffix drift, accents = same-entity. Different company or person names = different-entity with document's value.

"Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" vs "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" — these are clearly not spelling drift; they are different company names (though same corporate lineage). Per the rules, verdict = "different-entity", best_value = "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH".

The why: The register holds the legacy name while the 2021 certificate reflects the company's current legal name after rebranding; certificate is the legal instrument, so use its name.
